Disclosed are a method and apparatus for recording, at a recording device, a media feed relating to a scene; receiving, at the recording device, a series of wireless synchronisation messages; recording, for each received message, a timestamp value indicating a time of receipt; and storing the timestamp values and the media feed.

Disclosed are a method and an apparatus in which a recording device captures a media stream associated with a scene, receives multiple wireless synchronisation signals, records a timestamp for each received signal representing the time at which that signal was received, and stores both the captured media stream and the timestamp data.

Also disclosed are a method and an apparatus for obtaining, from each of two recording devices, the media stream recorded by that device together with a sequence of timestamp values. Each timestamp value identifies when a corresponding wireless synchronisation signal in a sequence was received by the relevant recording device. The timestamp sequence from the first recording device is then matched with the timestamp sequence from the second recording device so that the media stream from the first device can be synchronised with the media stream from the second device.
outputs.L3:
A recording device is used to capture a media feed relating to a scene. The media feed may include, for example, video, audio, or a combination of both, depending on the type of recording device and the nature of the scene being recorded.

While recording the media feed, the recording device receives a series of wireless synchronisation messages. These synchronisation messages may be transmitted periodically or at predetermined intervals and are used to provide a common timing reference for one or more recording devices operating in the same environment.

For each synchronisation message that is received, the recording device records and stores a timestamp value. Each timestamp value indicates the time at which the corresponding synchronisation message was received by that particular recording device. These timestamp values are stored in association with the recorded media feed so that they can later be used to determine the timing relationship between the media feed and the synchronisation messages.

Media feeds and their corresponding timestamp values are then received from multiple recording devices. Each recording device may have captured the scene from a different position, angle, or perspective, and each may have independently recorded the receipt times of the same or related wireless synchronisation messages.

The timestamp values from the different recording devices are compared and aligned in order to synchronise the respective media feeds. By aligning the timestamp values corresponding to the synchronisation messages, timing differences between the recording devices can be identified and compensated for. As a result, the media feeds from the multiple recording devices can be synchronised with one another, enabling coordinated playback, editing, analysis, or combination of the captured media.
outputs.L4:
A method and apparatus are provided for synchronizing media recordings captured by multiple recording devices. Each recording device records a media feed of a scene, such as video, audio, or combined audiovisual content, while also receiving wireless synchronization messages transmitted during the recording period. When a synchronization message is received, the recording device records a timestamp indicating the time at which that message was received. The device stores the recorded media feed together with the set of timestamps corresponding to the received synchronization messages.

In one implementation, a synchronization source periodically transmits wireless messages that can be received by any recording device within range. These messages may include identifying information, sequence numbers, timing information, or other data that allows each message to be distinguished from other messages. Each recording device uses its own local clock to timestamp the receipt of the messages. As a result, even if the devices do not share a common clock, each device produces a timestamp record that reflects when the same synchronization messages were received relative to its own recorded media.

After recording, the timestamp sets from two or more recording devices are compared. Because the devices received the same or corresponding wireless synchronization messages, the timestamps can be matched across devices. The differences between the matched timestamps are used to determine the temporal offset, drift, or other timing relationship between the devices’ local recording timelines. Using this timing relationship, the recorded media feeds can be aligned with one another.

Once aligned, the media feeds may be played back in synchronization, edited together, analyzed jointly, or otherwise processed as coordinated recordings of the same scene. For example, video captured from different camera angles may be synchronized for multi-camera playback, or audio and video recorded on separate devices may be aligned accurately without requiring a physical connection between the devices. The system therefore enables synchronization of recordings made by independent devices using wireless messages and locally stored receipt timestamps.

A method and its proper application can make the difference between confusion and clear progress. Whether in science, education, business, or daily life, a method provides structure. It helps people understand what needs to be done, in what order, and for what purpose.

A good method begins with a clear goal. Once the goal is defined, the next step is to gather information, choose the right tools, and follow a logical process. This makes tasks easier to manage and results easier to measure. Without a method, people may waste time, repeat mistakes, or overlook important details.

A method and consistent practice also help improve skills over time. For example, a student who uses a study method can learn more effectively than one who studies without a plan. Similarly, a business that follows a clear method for solving problems can make better decisions and achieve stronger results.

In short, a method is more than just a set of steps. It is a way to organize thinking, reduce uncertainty, and reach a desired outcome. When used carefully, a method and a clear purpose can lead to success in many areas of life.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for an invention that synchronizes media recordings from multiple devices using timestamps of received wireless synchronization messages.
counterfactuals.output: A method, apparatus, and computer-readable medium are provided for synchronizing media recordings captured by a plurality of recording devices. A wireless synchronization message is transmitted to the recording devices during a recording session, and each recording device records media data together with a timestamp indicating a local time at which the wireless synchronization message was received. The recorded media data and corresponding timestamps are obtained from the recording devices, and relative timing offsets among the media recordings are determined based at least in part on the timestamps of receipt of the wireless synchronization message. The media recordings are then temporally aligned using the determined timing offsets to generate synchronized media output. In some implementations, multiple wireless synchronization messages are transmitted and timestamped to improve alignment accuracy, compensate for clock drift, or identify timing irregularities among the recording devices.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise "method and apparatus are disclosed" summary for a system where recording devices capture video/audio and log receipt times of wireless sync beacons, then a server aligns the recordings.
counterfactuals.output: A method and apparatus are disclosed for synchronizing recordings from multiple recording devices. Each recording device captures at least one of video or audio data and logs receipt times of wireless synchronization beacons transmitted during recording. The recorded media and corresponding beacon timing logs are provided to a server, which compares the logged beacon receipt times among the devices to determine relative timing offsets. The server applies the timing offsets to align the recordings and generate synchronized media output.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a patent abstract describing recording a media feed at a device, storing timestamps for wireless synchronization messages, and synchronizing feeds from two recording devices based on those timestamp sets.
counterfactuals.output: A device records a media feed while wirelessly exchanging synchronization messages with at least one other recording device. During recording, the device stores a set of timestamps corresponding to transmission, receipt, or other timing events associated with the synchronization messages. A synchronization system obtains first and second recorded media feeds from respective recording devices, along with corresponding first and second timestamp sets. The system determines a temporal offset, clock relationship, or alignment function between the devices based on the timestamp sets, and synchronizes the recorded media feeds according to the determined relationship. The synchronized feeds may be combined, edited, played back, or otherwise processed with improved temporal alignment despite independent device clocks and wireless communication delays.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Create an invention disclosure abstract for synchronising multiple recorded media streams using wireless synchronisation messages received during capture and stored time stamp values.
counterfactuals.output: An invention is disclosed for synchronising multiple recorded media streams captured by separate recording devices. During capture, each device receives one or more wireless synchronisation messages from a common timing source or peer device. The device associates received synchronisation information with locally captured media by storing timestamp values, such as local clock values, media presentation times, or frame/sample identifiers, corresponding to reception of the synchronisation messages. After recording, the stored timestamp values and synchronisation-message data are used to determine temporal offsets, drift, or clock relationships among the devices. The recorded media streams are then aligned by adjusting playback timing, media timestamps, frame positions, sample positions, or edit points based on the determined timing relationships. The technique enables accurate post-capture synchronisation of audio, video, sensor, or other time-dependent media streams without requiring a continuous wired connection or continuous shared clock during recording.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
